paper_metadata.title: An introduction to financial option pricing on a qudit-based quantum computer

experiments.description: Numerical simulation of a qudit-based European call option pricing pipeline using a Black-Scholes-Merton log-normal asset distribution, Householder state preparation, qudit comparator/payoff encoding, and maximum-likelihood amplitude estimation without phase estimation.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation (maximum-likelihood estimation) applied to qudit-based option pricing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Estimate theta_P1 by maximizing the likelihood over theta in [0, pi/2]

hyperparameters.payoff_encoding: controlled-Y rotations with shift/scale c and s=pi/4

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Not reported; likelihood maximization over theta_P1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A single asset price distribution is discretized over dn points using n qudits of dimension d; basis state |i> encodes sampled asset value s_i via s_i = Smin + (i + 1/2)omega. The probability amplitudes sqrt(p_i) are loaded into the qudit register. A comparator qubit marks whether i >= k for strike K, and a payoff qubit encodes the shifted/scaled payoff via controlled RY rotations.
problem_formulation.objective_function: European call payoff f(ST)=max(0, ST-K); estimate expected payoff nu = e^{-rT} E_P[f(ST)]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints; truncation of the asset domain to [Smin, Smax] and discretization to dn points
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: At least 2 ancilla qubits are used in the main circuit: one comparator qubit and one payoff qubit; additional carry ancillas are used in the comparator subroutine but the exact count depends on the chosen comparator implementation

problem_instance.description: Single-asset European call option under the BSM model; simulation shown for two parameter sets and varying qudit dimension d.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic log-normal distribution from the BSM model; Fig. 6 uses S0=2.0, t=365/365, alpha=0.07, sigma=0.3, strike K=1.7; Fig. 7 uses S0=3.0, sigma=0.5, strike K=2.2. Asset domain truncated to three standard deviations around the mean and discretized into dn points.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Main register: n qudits plus 2 qubits (comparator and payoff); Fig. 6 explicitly uses a single asset qudit register with n=1 and Hilbert space dimension d=8 in the distribution plot, and the payoff-vs-d plot varies d. Exact total qubit-equivalent count is not reported.
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Not explicitly reported; the paper states the comparator can be O(n) depth with O(n) carry ancillas or at least O(n^2) depth with O(1) carry ancillas, and the overall amplitude-estimation loop uses T=7 with m_l=2^(l-1).

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Sample the BSM log-normal distribution, truncate to [Smin, Smax], discretize into dn points, normalize probabilities, compute strike index k, build Householder state-preparation matrix, and construct comparator/payoff subcircuits.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Use maximum-likelihood estimation on measurement counts to estimate theta_P1, map theta_P1 to P1, then recover expected payoff via Eq. 15 and discount to obtain option value.

speedup_claims.conditions: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation; asymptotic regime in number of oracle calls M
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes this is a theoretical scaling claim; practical NISQ hardware noise and circuit depth may limit realization.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation scales as O(M^-1) error in the number of oracle calls M; state preparation and arbitrary unitary compilation are discussed as O(nd^n) primitive operations for qudit systems under straightforward decomposition.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical Monte Carlo error scales as O(M^-1/2)
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: M = sum_{l=0}^T N(2m_l+1), with m_l = 2^(l-1) for l>=1 and m0=0

experiments.description: Scalability simulation of the same qudit-based European call pricing pipeline as a function of asset-register Hilbert space dimension d, comparing quantum simulation, finite-resource classical discretization, and analytic payoff.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation without phase estimation (maximum-likelihood estimation) applied to qudit-based option pricing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Estimate theta_P1 by maximizing the likelihood over theta in [0, pi/2]

hyperparameters.payoff_encoding: controlled-Y rotations with shift/scale c and s=pi/4

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Single-asset BSM distribution discretized into dn points; varying d changes the granularity of the encoded distribution and the total Hilbert space dimension.
problem_formulation.objective_function: European call payoff f(ST)=max(0, ST-K); estimate expected payoff nu = e^{-rT} E_P[f(ST)]
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Truncation to three standard deviations around the mean and discretization to finite d
problem_formulation.num_ancilla_qubits: Comparator and payoff qubits, plus comparator carry ancillas

problem_instance.description: Same single-asset European call option as exp_1, evaluated across different qudit dimensions d to study convergence toward the classical finite-resource result and analytic payoff.

dataset_specification.description: BSM synthetic distribution; Fig. 6b compares analytic payoff, classical finite-register payoff, and quantum simulation as d increases. The figure caption states a single asset qudit register with Hilbert space dimension d.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: Single asset register with n=1 qudit; exact d varies across the sweep. Comparator and payoff qubits are present. Exact qubit-equivalent count is not reported.
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Not explicitly reported; same amplitude-estimation loop with T=7 and comparator/payoff subcircuits

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: For each d, discretize the BSM distribution, compute the classical finite-resource payoff, and run the same quantum pipeline.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare quantum estimated payoff against classical finite-resource payoff and analytic payoff.

speedup_claims.conditions: Same amplitude-estimation-without-phase-estimation framework; asymptotic in oracle calls M
speedup_claims.caveats: This experiment is a scaling study over Hilbert space dimension d, not a direct runtime benchmark.
